V v explosive Saurav Das (@SauravDassss) #ImportantNews: The controversy over the alleged Delhi liquor-scam case before Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma is no longer confined to courtroom conduct alone. Now more troubling questions of proximity, patronage, conflict-of-interest, and the appearance of bias have come to light. Several of the 23 dischargees in the case had formally sought Justice Sharma’s recusal from hearing the CBI’s challenge to their discharge. Even then, the judge has so far resisted calls to step aside, even as former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal himself appears in person to argue the recusal application. Arguments are now scheduled for Monday, 13 April 2026. In my last Case In Point column for @frontline_india, I had already revealed, through an analysis of all the 165 criminal revision petitions of the same category as Kejriwal’s case, that Justice Sharma clearly departed from her usual pattern of handling such matters and had taken an unusually strange interest in this case. That, along with many other details that if read in singularity can be met with a shrug, but when read together, reveals a troubling pattern and credible fears of apprehension of bias in the liquor case. These by itself had raised serious questions. You may read my piece here: frontline.thehindu.com/colum… What has surfaced now makes those questions HARDER to dismiss. Justice Sharma’s son and daughter—Ishaan Sharma and Shambhavi Sharma—have both been empanelled by the Union government before the Delhi High Court and the Supreme Court. According to the empanelment details, both siblings were appointed on the very same days: 11 September 2025 for the Delhi High Court panels and 21 November 2025 for the Supreme Court panels. 1. Ishaan Sharma holds panels before both courts, including the highest Group A panel before the Supreme Court and Senior Panel Counsel status before the Delhi High Court. 2. Shambhavi Sharma, with mere four years of enrolment as advocate, too holds panels before both courts: Group C before the Supreme Court and Government Pleader before the Delhi High Court. 3. Ishaan Sharma also held a panel in the Delhi Development Authority (DDA), under the Union Housing Ministry, till at least 2024 (Check: sci.gov.in/sci-get-pdf/?diar…). 4. He also held a panel in the Delhi State Legal Services Authority since 2021 until at least the end of 2024 (Check: cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s395b7…). Panel counselship is among the most coveted forms of government legal patronage in the system. Ask any advocate and they will tell you how through these positions, the government allocates litigation, visibility, professional standing, and income. But the more important and troubling part is that they are positions held at the pleasure of the very government whose top law officers are now appearing before Justice Sharma in one of the most politically explosive cases in the country. And that is where the conflict sharpens. Of course, one need not prove an explicit bargain but justice must also be SEEN to be done, especially when it is a case of public interest. The test for seeking recusal of a judge is whether there exists a reasonable apprehension of bias and whether public confidence in the fairness of the process has been impaired. Like I had explained in my column, Indian law on recusal has long recognised that what matters is not just actual bias, but whether a litigant could REASONABLY FEEL that justice may NOT appear to be done. Here, several of the 23 dischargees feel justice may not be done impartially. And now this issue of one advocate, who happens to be the son of a judge, accumulating large number of panels within a relatively short post-enrolment period as an advocate. Ask any lawyer and they will tell you how many more accomplished, brilliant persons, with many more years as an advocate have failed to secure a panel through the formal process. The concerns are many. In this case, the question is whether a judge can continue to hear a politically sensitive challenge brought by the CBI, while her kin hold multiple Union government panels and receive work from the same legal establishment whose top officers allocate cases to them and are now appearing before her? Note this: as per one RTI reply I received, Ishaan Sharma was allocated 2,487 cases in 2023, 1,784 cases in 2024, and 1,633 cases in 2025. In both 2024 and 2025, he was allocated more case files than even Zoheb Hossain, the top, most publicly visible Enforcement Directorate lawyer—by 91 in 2024 and by 582 in 2025. This of course suggests the sustained and substantial allocation of state work before the son. The allocation is done by the topmost in the legal system. Also, this is not the first time that such questions of potential conflict of interest have arisen. In September 2024, I had highlighted the case of Padmesh Mishra, whose appointments across multiple union government and Rajasthan government positions drew scrutiny after his father, Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra, was elevated to the Supreme Court. Check: nitter.perennialte.ch/SauravDassss/status/18… The unease then was the same as it is now: when the children of sitting judges begin to accumulate government panels and positions in unusual concentration, something a regular lawyer, perhaps much more brilliant and of more history of practice, can only dream of, particularly after or around the parent’s rise within the judiciary, the issue is of institutional credibility. And no one really needs to state that that credibility is already under strain. Recently, Justice Manmohan of the Supreme Court himself publicly flagged corruption in the appointment of panel counsels by the Union government, questioning whether such appointments are really being made on merit at all. In a system where even a sitting Supreme Court judge is warning that panel-counsel appointments may be infected by extraneous considerations, the appearance of conflict in the present case becomes still harder to shrug away. Check: nitter.perennialte.ch/barandbench/status/203… Seen in that light, the present controversy is again not whether Justice Sharma is actually biased. It is about whether the institution can credibly insist that there is nothing to see here. The CBI has just filed an affidavit supporting Justice Sharma. A judge who I have documented, as per her own orders, to show unusual interest in a politically sensitive matter now finds herself in a position where her own kind hold/held as many as SIX government panels between them, while their bosses continue to appear before her. Even if one were to assume the absence of any actual impropriety, does this arrangement augur well for the appearance of judicial independence, especially in this case? The question is whether this not enough evidence of apprehension of bias that should suffice for a recusal. That is the question the High Court ought to have confronted with seriousness. Instead, by resisting recusal in these circumstances, the judge is unfortunately deepening this very suspicion that it should have avoided at all costs, or at least for the sake of institution. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/SauravDassss/status/2042148747568898432#m

Each March, mushers and sled dogs prepare to travel one of Alaska’s most historic winter routes during the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race. The trail itself isn’t permanent. It takes shape each winter. The depth, density, and timing of snowpack determine when a winter trail can safely take shape across public lands, including sections managed by the Bureau of Land Management. Small shifts in temperature can mean thinner snow at lower elevations or earlier melt in key sections. In fact, low snow has forced the Iditarod to move its starting location in 2003, 2015, 2017, and again in 2025. USGS scientists track snow conditions from satellites and in the field to better understand how Alaska’s winter landscape changes from year to year. By race day, winter has already built the trail across Alaska’s public lands. 📷: Landsat 9 image of Anchorage, Alaska, captured November 20, 2021. @BLMNational @BLMAlaska

Cette enquête inédite met en lumière le rôle central de Sipan Hemo dans la recomposition sécuritaire et politique du Nord-Est syrien. Elle analyse les défis auxquels il est confronté, entre intégration des forces kurdes, tensions régionales et rivalités internes, tout en soulignant son profil pragmatique et sa capacité à naviguer dans un environnement complexe. turkish intelligence (@turkish_intell) Sipan Hemo: From the YPG to a Central Figure in Syria’s New Architecture 1/2 The appointment of Sipan Hemo as Deputy Minister of Defense for northeastern Syria, officially confirmed on March 10, immediately places him at the center of major security and political challenges. A former Commander-in-Chief of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), he is now tasked with a particularly sensitive mission: integrating Kurdish forces into the military apparatus of the new Syrian regime, while managing an unstable regional environment marked by tensions between Iran and Israel. From the very first weeks of his tenure, Hemo has been confronted with a series of attacks targeting military positions in the region. On March 29, the Qasrak base, located in the Kurdish governorate of Hasakah, was struck by drones launched from the Iraqi border. A few days earlier, on March 23, the Kharab al-Jir base had also come under rocket fire, though no casualties were reported, notably due to the prior withdrawal of U.S. forces in February. Hemo was quick to respond publicly, accusing Baghdad, via his new account on X, of failing to effectively control its territory. Now responsible for the Kurdish regions from a military standpoint, he must secure an area still exposed to incursions by pro-Iranian Iraqi militias, particularly active in the context of the conflict opposing Tehran and Tel Aviv since late February. Although relatively spared so far, eastern Syria remains vulnerable to these regional dynamics. Beyond the security dimension, however, Sipan Hemo plays a central role in a long-term political process: the integration of Kurdish forces into Syrian state structures. This project, formalized by an agreement concluded on January 29, had been negotiated following the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024. At the time, Hemo was part of the team led by Mazloum Abdi, tasked with representing Kurdish interests vis-à-vis the new authorities in Damascus. This integration dynamic has also been reflected in symbolic appointments, such as that of Nourredin Issa Ahmed, a former SDF commander, who became governor of Hasakah in February, a first for a Kurd in Syria. However, this process unfolds in a personally difficult context for Hemo, marked by the death of his long-time ally Saleh Muslim, who passed away on March 11 in Erbil and was also expected to play a role in the new security architecture. On the ground, tensions remain high. Prior to the ceasefire negotiated under the auspices of U.S. envoy Tom Barrack, clashes between the SDF and forces stemming from Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), led by Ahmed al-Charaa, were nearly constant. In this context, Sipan Hemo’s profile appears to be an asset. Considered moderate and pragmatic, he embodies a conciliatory approach, in contrast to more controversial figures such as Azad Simi, head of SDF intelligence, who is viewed as too polarizing, particularly by Ankara. I must recommend Danny (@citrinowicz) as one of the most informed, unbiased and quite objective analysts in the realm of geopolitics and war in the Middle East. Danny forewarned the U.S. and Israel both not to be trapped by wishful thinking of a weakened Iran. Iran has lived under maximum sanctions for over 47 years and learned adaptation under a condition of near autarky. Iran hasn’t not traded with the U.S. and the Western world and their allies in this long period. Their international linkages are very limited and their trading partners include mainly China, Russia and South Africa. Others are trivial. The outside world knows littler about their real economy, industrial structure, technological progress and international trade and capital flows. Yes, the IMF balance of payment (BOP) statistics show a bleak outlook of Iran’s external account imbalances and currency volatility; it is however misleading if the real economy is mostly independent and insulated from the rest of world. Iran is a vast country with 92 million population and a history of 5,000 years of existence. Those who want to dismantle Iran as a sovereign country are fooling themselves. The world community needs a permanent peace in the Middle East. Danny (Dennis) Citrinowicz ,داني سيترينوفيتش (@citrinowicz) Iran Has Not Been Deterred — It Has Adapted By any conventional measure, the recent military campaign against Iran and its regional network was meant to reshape Tehran’s calculus. It has not. If anything, Iran has emerged more convinced that its long-standing strategy, anchored in regional proxies, calibrated escalation, and strategic patience remains effective. At the core of Iran’s thinking is a simple principle: commitment to the “Axis of Resistance” is not ideological excess; it is strategic insurance. By sustaining Hezbollah and other partners, Tehran ensures that it is never isolated in moments of crisis. That logic has not weakened under pressure, it has hardened. This explains Iran’s current behavior. On one hand, it is pushing to incorporate Hezbollah into any ceasefire framework, seeking to legitimize its most powerful proxy as a central actor in regional diplomacy. On the other, it continues measured offensive actions, carefully calibrated to maintain leverage without triggering full-scale war. This is not contradiction; it is strategy. At the same time, Iran is expanding the playing field. Its signaling around the Strait of Hormuz is not juat rhetoric but it is a reminder that escalation is not confined to Israel’s northern border. Global energy markets, maritime security, and economic stability are all part of Tehran’s deterrence toolkit. By linking local conflict to global consequences, Iran increases the cost of diplomatic failure. For Washington, this presents a familiar but sharpened dilemma. Israel, for both political and military reasons, is unlikely to significantly reduce operations in Lebanon in the near term. Yet without some degree of de-escalation, diplomacy has little chance of gaining traction. The likely result is growing U.S. pressure to slow the pace of military activity, not through formal constraints, but through quiet coordination aimed at buying time for negotiations. Here lies the strategic trap. Iran is betting it can manage escalation while advancing diplomacy on its own terms. It is unlikely to concede ground on its regional posture or its support for proxies, areas it views as essential to deterrence. However, it may show flexibility on the nuclear file, particularly enriched uranium levels, if the prize is meaningful sanctions relief. This creates a difficult choice for the United States: accept a deal that looks strikingly similar to what was available before the escalation, or reject it and risk a broader confrontation with far higher stakes. Neither option is attractive. But postponing the decision may be the most dangerous course of all. The key point is this - military pressure has not fundamentally altered Iran’s negotiating position. Tehran is not acting like a state under duress. It is acting like a state that believes time, leverage, and controlled risk are on its side. #IranWar‌ — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/citrinowicz/status/2042142949446685060#m

Open letter to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshall Asim Munir ; Cease fire in the Iran war has brought a sense of relief around the world. We hope and pray that this ceasefire will convert into a sustainable permanent peace agreement. The role Pakistan has played in making the ceasefire possible has been admired globally. Your leadership role in Pakistans efforts to make this possible is highly commendable and appreciated. More than anything else, this ceasefire and the extremely positive reaction around the world including the global financial and commodity markets, shows the dividends that peace and stability bring. The global acclaim and the increased relevance of Pakistan is an incredible opportunity. An opportunity that we must build upon. This will require sustained focused efforts in all spheres of state and society to carry out a national reconstruction which leads us towards security and prosperity. The most vital and urgent of these efforts has to be to bring peace and stability within Pakistan. We have extreme polarization in our polity ,and a trust deficit between state and citizen which is at dangerous levels. If this is not addressed, fear is that the opportunity that has been created will be transient, and we will once again be left to rue what could have been. Without wasting any time, an initiative should be taken to create a consensus on how to move the country forward in a manner that all the key stakeholders, and most importantly the people of Pakistan believe in and endorse. The PM should announce this initiative and it should have the following core elements. 1)Release of Imran Khan and all other political prisoners 2)Initiation of a dialogue of all political parties to work out a new charter of democracy 3)An agreement on timetable for next elections and reforms, including a reconstitution of the Election Commission and a code of conduct for all political parties in this interim period, which should take place before the country holds the next election 4)An agreement on the Governance structure until these next elections are held. All the above must be done within the bounds of the constitution, recognizing that the ultimate power in the country belongs to the people of Pakistan. Pakistanis want the national leadership to rise to the occasion, above personal and even institutional interest, and truly set a new path of progress and inclusive development. I truly believe that those leaders who shall be a part of this national reconstruction agreement will have their names etched in history as the men and women, who once and for all, set Pakistan on the path the founders led by Quaide azam envisioned when the country was founded. May Allah guide you in taking decisions which are in the best interest of the people of Pakistan. Regards Asad Umar

Last weekend, the Tech and Policy cohort tackled a complex and politically charged issue in Indian agriculture: formulating a comprehensive national policy for Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs). India’s farmers are facing mounting pressures from climate change, stagnating yields, and rising input costs. While GM crops could offer climate resilience and better nutrition, their adoption is stalled by a massive public trust deficit, environmental concerns, and a sluggish regulatory framework. With the Supreme Court recently directing the government to formulate a clear national policy, our cohort stepped into the shoes of expert consultants to crack the code. After intense debate and research, the cohort arrived at some promising solutions along these lines. 🏛️A Phased, Risk-Adjusted Framework: Moving away from binary approvals to a science-based, tiered regulatory system. This allows for the progressive expansion of GM commercialisation across vital food, oilseed, and pulse crops. 🏛️Regulatory Overhaul: Proposing an institutional overhaul to build regulatory capacity to bridge the trust gap through stakeholder engagement and evidence based decision making. 🪴Special Agricultural Zones: Creating agricultural equivalents of technology sandboxes that allows controlled fast tracked experimentation across the life cycle of GM crops. 🌍Leveraging the IP of India's vast crop diversity: An innovative solution that bypasses the domestic social and regulatory frictions by focussing on global licensing of the IP of India's vast biodiversity of germplasm. Every iteration of the workshop brings with it participants from varying backgrounds working together to solve complex policy problems. By going through a rigorous 11-week course prior, and learning how to critically think about ethics, economic reasoning, tech geopolitics, and policy-analysis. 🇺🇸🇪🇺🇮🇷 | La Maison-Blanche prépare un plan contre des alliés jugés peu coopératifs La Maison-Blanche envisage un plan visant à sanctionner certains alliés de l’OTAN que le président américain Donald Trump estime ne pas avoir soutenu les États-Unis et Israël durant la guerre en Iran. La proposition inclut la possibilité de redéployer des troupes américaines hors des pays jugés peu coopératifs, tels que l’Espagne, l’Allemagne, l’Italie et la France, pour les repositionner vers des pays considérés comme plus favorables, notamment en Europe de l’Est. Le plan en est encore à un stade préliminaire, mais il gagne en soutien auprès de hauts responsables. (WSJ)

🇺🇸🇮🇷 | NYT : Le président américain Donald Trump est intervenu lors d’une réunion consacrée aux négociations de cessez-le-feu avec l’Iran, en détaillant le nombre de ponts et de centrales électriques qu’il se disait prêt à cibler. Il a indiqué à ses conseillers que le gouvernement iranien porterait la responsabilité si des frappes américaines venaient à tuer des civils iraniens rassemblés à proximité de ces infrastructures. Avant l’annonce de l’accord de cessez-le-feu conclu in extremis, des discussions progressaient discrètement, la haute direction semblant donner son aval à la poursuite des négociations lundi. Toutefois, dès mardi matin, la Maison-Blanche a manifesté des signes d’impatience, conduisant Donald Trump à publier une menace à l’encontre de l’Iran. Cette déclaration a suscité la colère des dirigeants iraniens qui, dénonçant des menaces visant des infrastructures critiques, ont transmis via le Pakistan un message indiquant la suspension des communications avec les États-Unis, estimant que leur contrôle du détroit d’Ormuz leur conférait un avantage stratégique. C’est finalement la Chine qui a permis de sortir de l’impasse diplomatique, en incitant l’Iran à considérer les conséquences économiques, notamment pour ses partenaires comme la Chine, d’un maintien de la fermeture du détroit.

🇮🇷🇺🇸 | Le trafic maritime à travers le détroit d’Ormuz est resté extrêmement limité mercredi, malgré l’appel du président Donald Trump à sa réouverture immédiate dans le cadre des conditions du cessez-le-feu. Le NJ Earth, naviguant sous pavillon grec, et le Daytona Beach, sous pavillon libérien, ont été les premiers navires à traverser le détroit d’Ormuz. L’incertitude dans le transport maritime demeure élevée, avec des informations selon lesquelles certains opérateurs ont payé des frais dépassant 1 million de dollars pour sécuriser leur passage, ce qui souligne les risques persistants pour les flux mondiaux d’énergie et de commerce. (WSJ)

CRPF शौर्य दिवस पर फोर्स के हमारे साहसी और वीर जवानों को हार्दिक बधाई और सादर नमन। आपका साहस और बलिदान हर दिन हमारे देश की रक्षा करता है। आप सीमाओं पर तैनात रहकर देश को सुरक्षित रखते हैं, आतंकवाद और नक्सलवाद से लोहा लेते हैं, और लोकतंत्र के सबसे बड़े उत्सव, चुनावों को शांतिपूर्ण और सुरक्षित बनाते हैं। लेकिन सच्ची श्रद्धांजलि केवल शब्दों से नहीं होती। वर्षों के त्याग, तपस्या और सेवा के बावजूद CAPF जवानों को न तो समय पर प्रमोशन मिलता है, न ही अपनी ही फोर्स का नेतृत्व करने का अधिकार - क्योंकि शीर्ष पद फ़ोर्स से बाहर के लोगों के लिए आरक्षित हैं। CAPF के जवान विशेष प्रशिक्षण, जमीनी अनुभव और गहरी रणनीतिक समझ रखते हैं - इसलिए राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा के नज़रिये से भी यह जरूरी है कि इन बलों का नेतृत्व उसी सिस्टम से आने वाले लोग करें, जो उनकी चुनौतियों और जरूरतों को सही मायनों में समझते हों। नेतृत्व के अवसरों से वंचित रखने से लेकर वेतन, कल्याण और सम्मान से जुड़े लंबे समय से लंबित मुद्दों तक - यह संस्थागत अन्याय उन जवानों के मनोबल को ठेस पहुंचाता है, जो अपना जीवन देश की सुरक्षा में समर्पित कर देते हैं। यह सिर्फ़ करियर का सवाल नहीं, बल्कि न्याय और सम्मान का मुद्दा है। मैं और कांग्रेस पार्टी आपका पूरा आदर और आपसे मोहब्बत करते हैं और ये मानते हैं कि अपने फ़ोर्स में आपकी तरक्की, शीर्ष नेतृत्व और सम्मान आपका हक है - हमारी सरकार आते ही इस भेदभावपूर्ण व्यवस्था को समाप्त किया जाएगा और CAPF जवानों को उनका पूरा अधिकार दिया जाएगा। देश आप वीरों का ऋणी है - अब समय है कि आपके साथ न्याय हो। जय हिंद! 🇮🇳

🚨📰 #USNAVY UPDATE: USS John P. Murtha to support NASA's Artemis II mission SAN DIEGO – Amphibious transport dock ship USS John P. Murtha (LPD 26) is slated to serve as the recovery ship for the Orion spacecraft and its crew upon their return from the historic Artemis II mission. The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft, sending four astronauts on an approximately 10-day journey that will take them beyond the Moon. This mission will mark humanity's first crewed voyage to the vicinity of the Moon in over 50 years. Upon completion of their mission, the Orion capsule will splash down in the Pacific Ocean, where John P. Murtha and its crew will be prepared to recover the astronauts and the spacecraft.

Emergence kicks in: the model starts recombining latent patterns into outputs that feel "new" because no single training example had them exactly. It's not invention from void—it's hyper-efficient compression revealing unseen connections in the data distribution. NITI Aayog released the second edition of the report “From Borrowers to Builders: Women and India’s Evolving Credit Market”. The report was prepared under the aegis of the Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP), by @TransUnion CIBIL and @MicroSave Consulting (MSC). The report highlights that women’s participation in India’s formal credit ecosystem has expanded significantly, with portfolios growing nearly five-fold since 2017 and 16 crore women now part of the system. This scale of engagement signals a shift in how women are accessing and using formal finance within India’s growth trajectory. Building on these findings, Nidhi Chhibber, CEO, NITI Aayog, underscored that the focus ahead must be on directing credit towards enterprise outcomes. She also highlighted embedding financial literacy across education and skilling systems as a core lever, alongside stronger alignment across ministries and institutions. This report draws on longitudinal credit bureau data covering approximately 16 crore (160 million) credit-active women, complemented by primary research with 161 rural nano-entrepreneurs, offering a robust blend of quantitative evidence and behavioural insights. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #WomenInFinance #FinancialInclusion #WomenEntrepreneurs #CreditAccess #Empowerment #WEP @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @suman_bery @annaroy9 @wep_community @MoHFW_INDIA @CimGOI @DPIITGoI @EduMinOfIndia @MSDE @SwapnaleeNITI @MSME @TransUnion @MicroSave

فرماندهی امنیه‌ی طالبان در فراه اعلام کرده‌ است که آتش‌سوزی گسترده‌ی بندر ابونصر فراهی در این ولایت به کمک ایران مهار شده است. منابع محلی روز گذشته (چهارشنبه، ۱۹ حمل) از آتش‌سوزی گسترده در بندر ابونصر فراهی در ولایت فراه گزارش داده بودند. فرماندهی امنیه‌ی طالبان در فراه نیز اعلام کرد که به‌دلیل بی‌احتیاطی کارکنان این بندر، تایرها دچار آتش‌سوزی شده بود. به‌گفته‌ی این فرماندهی، این آتش‌سوزی در نتیجه‌ی اقدام به‌ موقع تیم آتش‌نشانی طالبان و با همکاری کشور همسایه، ایران، به‌طور کامل مهار شده است. فرماندهی امنیه‌ی طالبان در فراه تا کنون درباره‌ی میزان خسارات ناشی از این آتش‌سوزی چیزی نگفته است.

On the Iditarod Trail, winter conditions can change mile by mile. River ice thickens and thins. Snow bridges form and collapse. Glaciers shift. What looks solid one day may change the next. USGS scientists study glacier movement and ice conditions across Alaska to better understand how these winter landscapes behave. Because when travel depends on frozen rivers and valleys, reading the landscape matters. 📸 1: Aerial photo showing fracture line of avalanche along a snow ridge line. A reminder of how quickly conditions can shift in steep terrain. 📸 2: Steam rises through fractured ice at Redoubt Volcano, where heat from below reshapes the frozen surface above. 📸 3: View of Nellie Juan Glacier from Wolverine Glacier, where visibility and weather can change in minutes. While China was busy shipping missile chemicals to Iran and collecting yuan tolls at Hormuz, someone was inside its most sensitive supercomputer stealing everything. CNN reports that a hacker group calling itself FlamingChina breached the China National Supercomputing Center in Tianjin and exfiltrated up to 10 petabytes of classified defence data. The samples posted on dark web forums include bomb and missile designs, animated explosion simulations, structural integrity tests, renderings of the J-20 stealth fighter, sixth-generation aircraft concepts, nuclear submarine schematics, hypersonic weapons systems, and target analyses for American assets including HIMARS launchers and carrier strike groups. Ten petabytes. For context, the entire printed collection of the US Library of Congress is approximately 10 terabytes. This breach is one thousand times that volume. It is being sold for cryptocurrency on Breach Forums. Cybersecurity experts who reviewed the previews told CNN the data appears genuine, matching known output patterns from the NSCC Tianjin facility, which serves over 6,000 clients including defence agencies and aviation firms across China. The timing is extraordinary. Trump posted a 50 percent tariff threat on any country supplying military weapons to Iran hours before CNN published this story. Five Chinese vessels shipped sodium perchlorate to Iran from Gaolan Port in the past six weeks, enough propellant precursor for hundreds of ballistic missiles. China’s ghost fleet continues operating through the IRGC’s yuan toll booth at Hormuz. And now the supercomputer that designed the weapons China is helping Iran reconstitute has been gutted by hackers selling its contents for the same cryptocurrency that Iran charges for strait passage. The irony is architectural. China built a parallel financial system using yuan and crypto to bypass the dollar at Hormuz. A hacker group is now using crypto to bypass Chinese state security and sell Beijing’s most classified military designs to anyone with a wallet address. The same technology that enables sanction evasion enables espionage monetisation. The blockchain does not distinguish between a toll payment and a weapons leak. It processes both. For Xi, this is a catastrophe arriving at the worst possible moment. Bessent’s mid-May Beijing summit was already going to be difficult. Trump holds the waiver on 140 million barrels of Chinese-bound Iranian crude. The 50 percent tariff threat targets China’s arms pipeline. The IDF just destroyed 100 Hezbollah targets using F-35I aircraft with Israeli software upgrades the Pentagon approved today. And now the classified designs for China’s most advanced military systems, the systems that justify the rare earth monopoly and the South China Sea posture and the Taiwan coercion campaign, are available for purchase on a dark web forum for less than the price of a single Hormuz transit. If the data is genuine, every adversary and ally of China can now reverse-engineer the capabilities Beijing spent decades and hundreds of billions developing. The J-20’s stealth profile. The hypersonic glide vehicle’s trajectory calculations. The nuclear submarine’s acoustic signature. The sixth-generation fighter’s sensor architecture. All of it, priced in crypto, available now. China wanted to build a post-dollar world. A hacker group just demonstrated what that world looks like when the technology works in both directions. open.substack.com/pub/shanak…

Any toll to pass through the Strait of Hormuz would not be “a beautiful thing,” as the president contended to ABC News Jonathan Karl. It would represent an unprecedented surrender of freedom of navigation, which the U.S. Navy has fought to preserve and protect since Thomas Jefferson was president. From the days of the Barbary pirates to the Somali pirates and the Houthis, the U.S. and its allies have contended that U.S. ships can sail wherever they want, whenever they want, in international waters, and no state, entity, or force gets to restrict that. The Strait of Hormuz is legally international waters. Neither Iran, nor Oman, nor the United States is legally permitted to charge a fee or threaten force against ships that do not pay a fee. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said the reason the U.S. was destroying the Iranian navy was to “ensure freedom of navigation.” If the U.S. had always been amenable to the Iranian regime charging a fee to all the tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz . . . why did we just fight this war?

I spoke today with Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian, as well as with U.S. President Donald Trump. I told both of them that their decision to accept a ceasefire was the best possible one. I expressed my hope that the ceasefire will be fully respected by each of the belligerents, across all areas of confrontation, including in Lebanon. This is a necessary condition for the ceasefire to be credible and lasting. It must open the way to comprehensive negotiations capable of ensuring security for all in the Middle East. Any agreement will have to address the concerns raised by Iran’s nuclear and ballistic missile programs, as well as its regional policy and its actions obstructing navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. This is how a strong and lasting peace can be built, with the support of all those who are able to contribute to it. France will play its full part, in close coordination with its partners in the Middle East. This is also what I discussed today in my exchanges with the leaders of Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Lebanon, and Iraq.

C’est ainsi qu’une paix robuste et durable pourra être bâtie, avec le concours de tous ceux qui peuvent y contribuer. La France y prendra toute sa part, en liaison étroite avec ses partenaires au Moyen-Orient. We've done some nice modernizations and improvements, fixed bugs, added features, updated the toolchain, and more. But our release is currently blocked by @Microsoft. The recent thread on Hacker News encouraged me to write this up, rather than just grumbling to myself privately about it as I have the last two weeks. I logged in to get the WireGuardNT driver signed -- a necessary step for driver authors -- and was greeted by this vague message that the account has been suspended. Looking further into it, it seems like they instituted an identity verification policy, didn't notify me about it, and then I guess they suspended accounts who didn't do the verification. So of course I did the ID card verification immediately, but now an appeal is necessary. The appeals process requires filing a support ticket, but filing a support ticket requires a non-suspended account... Catch-22, eventually resolved by filing one through Azure and getting it rerouted to the right department. That was two weeks ago. Now they've told me there's a 60 day appeal review period. Wish us luck! It's a little crazy, because what if there was some critical ring 0 RCE vuln that was being exploited in the wild and that needed to be patched immediately? (Just hypothetical; there isn't.) In that case, telling users "sorry, you've got to wait 60 days" would be sort of bad. And users of WireGuard for Windows are also Microsoft Windows users, so I can't see how this is good for Microsoft either. I think it must just be a case of bureaucracy gone slightly off the rails. व्हिजन ते अंमलबजावणी; विकसित महाराष्ट्राचा आराखडा साकार मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली आज मुंबई येथे 'विकसित महाराष्ट्र व्हिजन 2047' च्या अंमलबजावणीचा आढावा घेण्यासाठी गठीत व्हिजन व्यवस्थापन नियामक मंडळाची बैठक पार पडली. देश आणि राज्यासाठी 2026 ते 2030 हा कालावधी अत्यंत महत्त्वाचा आहे. या काळात योग्य निर्णय आणि अंमलबजावणीच्या माध्यमातून महाराष्ट्राला केवळ मोठी अर्थव्यवस्था नव्हे, तर दरडोई उत्पन्नात महाराष्ट्राला अग्रेसर राज्य बनविणे शक्य होणार आहे. त्यादृष्टीने महाराष्ट्राच्या दीर्घकालीन प्रगतीसाठी तयार करण्यात आलेल्या 'विकसित महाराष्ट्र 2047' या महत्त्वाकांक्षी व्हिजनच्या प्रभावी अंमलबजावणीसाठी पुढील चार वर्षांत 2030 पर्यंत मोजता येण्याजोगी उद्दिष्टे साध्य करण्यावर विभागांनी भर द्यावा, असे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी दिले. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, व्हिजनच्या अंमलबजावणीसाठी राज्य शासनाने 'व्हिजन मॅनेजमेंट युनिट' स्थापन करून प्रत्येक विभागासोबत सखोल चर्चा केली आहे. त्यानुसार 2030 पर्यंत साध्य करता येतील, अशा उद्दिष्टांचे स्पष्ट विभाजन करण्यात आले आहे. राज्याच्या विकासासाठी प्रगत जिल्ह्यांमध्ये नव्या तंत्रज्ञानाच्या आधारे अधिक वेगाने वाढ करणे आणि उर्वरित 11 जिल्ह्यांमध्ये मोठ्या प्रमाणावर विकासकामांची संधी आहे, त्यावर काम करण्याचे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी दिले. हेच जिल्हे पुढील काळात राज्याच्या वाढीचे प्रमुख केंद्र ठरू शकतात. विभागांनी तयार केलेले ॲक्शन प्लॅन हे केवळ महत्त्वाकांक्षी नसून ते अचूक, कालबद्ध, मोजता येण्यायोग्य (specific, measurable, time-bound) असणे आवश्यक आहे. चार वर्षांत 100 टक्के उद्दिष्टपूर्ती साध्य करण्याच्या दृष्टीने प्रत्येक विभागाने आपल्या कामाच्या स्पष्ट कालमर्यादा आणि निर्देशक निश्चित करावेत, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी निर्देश दिले. या व्हिजनसाठी उपलब्ध निधीमध्येच काम करून नव्या कार्यपद्धतीचा वापर करत अपेक्षित परिणाम साध्य केले गेले पाहिजेत. त्याचबरोबर, केंद्र सरकारच्या योजनांमधून (Central Sector आणि Centrally Sponsored Schemes) जास्तीत जास्त निधी मिळवण्यासाठी विभागांनी सक्रिय प्रयत्न करावेत, असे निर्देशही मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी दिले. PPP, ADB, World Bank यांसारख्या विविध स्रोतांमधून निधी मिळवण्यासाठी सक्षम आणि तयार प्रकल्प आवश्यक आहेत. तसेच धोरण जाहीर केल्यानंतर सहा महिने आणि वर्षभरानंतर त्याचा प्रत्यक्ष परिणाम तपासला पाहिजे. धोरण निर्मिती आणि अंमलबजावणीच्या परिणामांचे मोजमाप आवश्यक आहे. यासाठी सर्व धोरणे मोजता येण्यायोग्य निर्देशकांवर आधारित असावीत, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले. सर्व विभागांनी आपले ॲक्शन प्लॅन वित्त विभागासोबत समन्वय साधून 30 एप्रिलपर्यंत अंतिम करावेत. पुढील काळात सर्व प्रगतीचे डायनॅमिक मॉनिटरिंग डॅशबोर्डद्वारे केले जाईल. यामुळे प्रत्येक विभागाच्या कामाची नियमित आणि पारदर्शक समीक्षा होईल. या आराखड्याची प्रभावी अंमलबजावणी हा आता पुढचा महत्वाचा टप्पा असणार आहे. 🚨📰 #USNAVY UPDATE: USS John P. Murtha to support NASA's Artemis II mission SAN DIEGO – Amphibious transport dock ship USS John P. Murtha (LPD 26) is slated to serve as the recovery ship for the Orion spacecraft and its crew upon their return from the historic Artemis II mission. The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft, sending four astronauts on an approximately 10-day journey that will take them beyond the Moon. This mission will mark humanity's first crewed voyage to the vicinity of the Moon in over 50 years. Upon completion of their mission, the Orion capsule will splash down in the Pacific Ocean, where John P. Murtha and its crew will be prepared to recover the astronauts and the spacecraft.
